exposure: Vaginal delivery vs. elective cesarean section
Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. elective cesarean section)
cohort: 95 pregnant women and their newborns (50 vaginal deliveries, 45 elective cesarean sections)
finding: While newborns delivered vaginally had higher levels of disulfide (-SS) in cord blood, suggesting greater oxidative stress, the overall dynamic thiol-disulfide homeostasis was similar between vaginal and cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Infants born vaginally may have more oxidative stress than those born via cesarean section, as evidenced by higher disulfide levels in cord blood.
